newsitem.title: USA: Fla. professor is first American to head Amnesty.
newsitem.headline: Fla. professor is first American to head Amnesty.

text.p: A Florida professor on Tuesday became the first American chairman of Amnesty International, the London-based human rights organisation and her university announced.
Susan Waltz, 45, a professor of international relations at Miami's Florida International University, has been involved with the organisation for 20 years, a joint news release said.
A professor at FIU since 1984, she has campaigned to free prisoners of conscience in Tunisia and other countries and worked to expose secret prisons in nations including Morocco.
Waltz will oversee the activities of Amnesty International's 64 national sections with more than 1.1 million members in 152 countries until the end of 1997.
She said one of her initial goals would be to expand the organisation's role in the southern hemisphere -- South America, Africa, Asia and the Middle East.

Amnesty International was founded in 1961 by Peter Benenson, a British attorney who was moved by a newspaper article about two young Portuguese students imprisoned after they were heard toasting freedom.
